subject: MAP Blueprint: kickoff draft & timeline options
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@pharmex.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: MAP Blueprint: kickoff draft & timeline options

Hi Alyssa —

Great to meet you and Tom on the call earlier. Thanks for the candid discussion about inference throughput needs and the regulatory constraints around PHI at Pharmex. Per our conversation, I put together an initial Mutual Action Plan (we're calling it a MAP blueprint) that outlines milestone options, recommended owners, and a couple of target-close scenarios so you can pick what fits your internal timing. I attached the workbook and a short PDF of my discovery notes.

High-level recap (from discovery):
- Primary use case: clinical summarization + embedding-based search for internal knowledge base.
- Traffic profile: bursts up to 200 req/min, median context ~2k tokens.
- Compliance: SOC 2 controls required; air-gapped option may be evaluated.
- Success criteria: latency p95 < 400ms, unit cost <$0.015/token for high-volume flows.

MAP blueprint — two timeline options (short summary):

Option A — Accelerated pilot (recommended if procurement can move quickly)
- Pilot duration: 6 weeks (pilot + integration + evaluation)
- Milestones: 1) Kickoff & environment access, 2) Model selection & config, 3) Integration + end-to-end tests, 4) Pilot evaluation & handoff
- Owners: Redwood (Camila, Sergio) / Pharmex (Alyssa)
- Target close (contract signature to enable production path): Oct 22, 2026

Option B — Phased rollout (lower ramp risk)
- Pilot + staged expansion over 10–12 weeks
- Additional milestone: security review + procurement PO cadence
- Target close: Nov 24, 2026

Dependencies / risks to call out:
- Procurement timeline / PO issuance
- SOC 2 evidence & security POC window
- Data access (sample records for latency testing)

Ask / next steps:
1) Please confirm the primary stakeholder roster for the project (names + roles) so I can lock owners into the MAP worksheet.
2) Tell us which timeline you prefer (Option A or B). If neither fits, propose a target week.
3) If Option A, can procurement confirm a PO path by Sep 21?

Proposed immediate scheduling: 60-min kickoff workshop the week of Sep 7 to align on access, security contacts, and data handoff. I'll draft a calendar once I hear your preferred option.

Attachments: Pharmex-MAP-blueprint-v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), discovery-notes-20260902.pdf (call notes)

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap and the workbook. Tom and I reviewed the MAP blueprint this morning. Quick notes from our side:

Stakeholder roster (please add these folks in the MAP):
- Alyssa Chen — Head of Data Science (primary stakeholder)
- Tom Pierce — VP Engineering (infrastructure approvals + procurement gate)
- Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@pharmex.com> — Security & Compliance (SOC 2)

We prefer Option A to keep momentum, but there are two constraints: 1) Procurement typically needs a statement of work + PO lead time (~2–3 weeks), and 2) Priya will need the SOC 2 evidence and a short security questionnaire answered before we can start any private deployment.

Can you do two things for us?
1) Add Priya to the MAP as the security owner and tag the SOC 2 evidence as a critical dependency.
2) Share a short checklist of required artifacts for the security review (SOC 2 report, data handling diagram, encryption/KMS approach).

If you can get the security checklist and the refreshed MAP with Priya listed, we'll aim for a kickoff workshop the week of Sep 14 (tomorrow is tight for us).

Also, attaching a procurement note: Tom indicates we must budget for a pilot license line and plan for early procurement engagement.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Alyssa

- Lock the kickoff for Tue, Sep 15 (I will send a calendar invite with objectives).
